Lisa — thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers up front, then a worked example attached. I also attached our latest pricing_slabs_v2.xlsx with the slab definitions we plan to apply.

High level:
- Sequencing window: we group per-user activity into a 2-minute sequencing window by default when requests are within that gap; longer idle gaps break the window and start a new billing window. This reduces double-counting for quick follow-ups but still charges minimums per active window.
- Rounding & minimums: token consumption is tallied per-window, fractional tokens (from sub-tokenization) are summed and then rounded up to the nearest whole token for metering. After token rounding, we apply the slab minimum for that window (e.g., minimum 1 unit = 100 tokens equivalent in this customer's mapping). Any shortfall is charged to meet the minimum slab for that window.

Worked example (attached as sample invoice lines):
- Session start 09:00:00; three active streams at 09:05, 09:15, 09:40 and a final summarization call at 09:45.
- Window grouping: Streams at 09:05 and 09:15 are >2 minutes apart, so they are two separate windows; 09:40 and 09:45 fall within 2 minutes and get grouped.
- Raw token counts (sub-token): 09:05 -> 312.7, 09:15 -> 128.3, 09:40 -> 421.6, 09:45 -> 210.2
- Token rounding: 313, 129, 422, 210
- Apply per-window minimum: if minimum maps to 150 tokens, then 129 becomes 150, 210 stays 210, etc. Line-level invoice shows both raw rounded tokens and post-minimum billed tokens.

Adding a few operational clarifications from the billing side so ACME can reconcile cleanly: 

- Sequencing window enforcement: it is evaluated on the server side using session_id + last_active timestamp. We will include last_active and window_id in invoice line metadata so your ledger can join on those fields when reconciling.
- Minimum slab mapping: Redwood offers two ways for enterprise customers — (A) token-minimum slab (our default) or (B) dollar-minimum slab mapped to seat/burst commitments. For ACME's pilot we've recommended token-minimum to keep math transparent.
- Rounding symmetry: to avoid disputes we round upward at metering and then show a counter line ("rounding credit") when cumulative rounding across a billing period exceeds a threshold (0.5% of billed tokens). That credit appears as a negative line on the invoice.

I've attached an internal sample invoice export that mirrors what we'll send to you. Chloe — if ACME signs the amendment, we should turn on the detailed invoice export for them (CSV with window_id, session_id, rounded_tokens, billed_tokens, rounding_credit).
